questions.q:
The light rays from an object have been reflected towards an observer from a standard flat mirror, the image observed by the observer are :-

A. Real

B. Erect

C. Smaller in size than object

D. Laterally inverted

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: Image formed by a plane mirror is always virtual, laterally inverted, erect image and of the same size as the object.

xy=f2

f=d1d2d1-d2

R=2f=2d1d2d1-d2

questions.q:
A light wave travelling linearly in a medium of dielectric constant 4, incidents on the horizontal interface separating medium with air. The angle of incidence for which the total intensity of incident wave will be reflected back into the same medium will be :
(Given : relative permeability of medium μr=1)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Relative refractive index is μ=μrεr=4×1=2

Now, for complete reflection, θ>θc, where, θc is critical angle.

Now, critical angle is sinθc=1μ=12

 ⇒θc=sin-112⇒θc=30°

So, the angle of incidence for which the total intensity of incident wave will be reflected back into the same medium is θ>30° i.e., 60°.

questions.q: At the interface between two materials having refractive indices \(n_1\) and \(n_2\), the critical angle for reflection of an em wave is \(\theta_{1 C}\). The \(n_2\) material is replaced by another material having refractive index \(n_3\) such that the critical angle at the interface between \(n_1\) and \(n_3\) materials is \(\theta_{2 \mathrm{C}}\). If \(\mathrm{n}_3\gt\mathrm{n}_2\gt\mathrm{n}_1 ; \frac{\mathrm{n}_2}{\mathrm{n}_3}=\frac{2}{5}\) and \(\sin \theta_{2 \mathrm{C}}-\sin \theta_{1 \mathrm{C}}=\frac{1}{2}\), then \(\theta_{1 \mathrm{C}}\) is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \sin \theta_{1 C}=\frac{n_1}{n_2} \\ & \sin \theta_{2 C}=\frac{n_1}{n_3} \\ & \sin \theta_{2 C}-\sin \theta_{1 C}=\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{n}_1 \frac{\mathrm{n}_2}{\mathrm{n}_3}-\frac{\mathrm{n}_1}{\mathrm{n}_2}=\frac{1}{2} \\ & \mathrm{n}_1 \frac{\mathrm{n}_2}{\mathrm{n}_3}-\mathrm{n}_1=\frac{\mathrm{n}_2}{2} \\ & \mathrm{n}_1\left(\frac{2}{5}-1\right)=\frac{\mathrm{n}_2}{2} \\ & \frac{\mathrm{n}_1}{\mathrm{n}_2}=\frac{-5}{6} \\ & =\sin ^{-1}\left(-\frac{5}{6}\right)\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Which of the following statement is correct?
options: In primary rainbow, observer sees red colour on the top and violet on the bottom
In primary rainbow, observer sees violet colour on the top and red on the bottom
In primary rainbow, light wave suffers total internal reflection twice before coming out of water drops
Primary rainbow is less bright than secondary rainbow.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
In primary rainbow, red colour is at top and violet is at bottom. The colours are in the order of violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange and red (VIBGYOR). Since violet colour has the smallest wavelength, in the primary rainbow, it suffers maximum refraction. That is why it appears on the innermost position.

Intensity of secondary rainbow is less in comparison to primary rainbow.

questions.q:
In finding out refractive index of glass slab the following observations were made through travelling microscope 50 vernier scale division $=49 \mathrm{MSD} ; 20$ divisions on main scale in each $\mathrm{cm}$
For mark on paper
$\mathrm{MSR}=8.45 \mathrm{~cm}, \mathrm{VC}=26$
For mark on paper seen through slab
MSR $=7.12 \mathrm{~cm}, V C=41$
For powder particle on the top surface of the glass slab
$\mathrm{MSR}=4.05 \mathrm{~cm}, \mathrm{VC}=1$
(MSR $=$ Main Scale Reading, VC $=$ Vernier Coincidence)
Refractive index of the glass slab is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & 1 \mathrm{MSD}=\frac{1 \mathrm{~cm}}{20}=0.05 \mathrm{~cm} \\ & 1 \mathrm{VSD}=\frac{49}{50} \mathrm{MSD}=\frac{49}{50} \times 0.05 \mathrm{~cm}=0.049 \mathrm{~cm} \\ & \mathrm{LC}=1 \mathrm{MSD}-1 \mathrm{VSD}=0.001 \mathrm{~cm} \end{aligned}$
For mark on paper, $\mathrm{L}_1=8.45 \mathrm{~cm}+26 \times 0.001 \mathrm{~cm}=84.76 \mathrm{~mm}$ For mark on paper through slab, $\mathrm{L} 2=7.12 \mathrm{~cm}+41 \times 0.001 \mathrm{~cm}=71.61 \mathrm{~mm}$ For powder particle on top surface, $\mathrm{ZE}=4.05 \mathrm{~cm}+1 \times 0.001 \mathrm{~cm}=40.51 \mathrm{~mm}$
$\begin{aligned} \therefore & \text { actual } \mathrm{L}_1=84.76-40.51=44.25 \mathrm{~mm} \\ & \text { actual } \mathrm{L}_2=71.61-40.51=31.10 \mathrm{~mm} \\ & \mathrm{~L}_2=\frac{\mathrm{L}_1}{\mu} \\ \Rightarrow & \mu=\frac{\mathrm{L}_1}{\mathrm{~L}_2}=\frac{44.25}{31.10}=1.42\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
Three rays of light, namely red R, green (G) and blue (B) are incident on the face PQ of a right angled prism PQR as shown in figure.

The refractive indices of the material of the prism for red, green and blue wavelength are 1.27,1.42 and 1.49 respectively. The colour of the ray(s) emerging out of the face PR is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Assuming that the right angled prism is an isoceles prism, so the other angles will be 45° each.

⇒ Each incident ray will make an angle of 45° with the normal at face PR.

⇒ The wavelength corresponding to which the incidence angle is less than the critical angle, will pass through PR.

⇒θC= critical angle

⇒θC=sin-11μ

⇒ If θC≥45°

the light ray will pass

⇒θCRed=sin-111.27=51.94°

Red will pass.

⇒θCGreen=sin-111.42=44.76°

Green will not pass

⇒θCBlue=sin-111.49=42.15°

Blue will not pass

⇒ So only red will pass through PR.

questions.q: An upright object is placed at a distance of <math><mn>40</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> in front of a convergent lens of focal length <math><mn>20</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo>.</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi></math> A convergent mirror of focal length <math><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mn>10</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> is placed at a distance of <math><mn>60</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> on the other side of the lens. The position and size of the final image will be:
options: <math><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mn>40</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi></math> from the convergent lens, twice the size of the object
<math><mn>20</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> from the convergent mirror, twice the size of the object

<math><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mn>40</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi></math> from the convergent lens, same size of the object

<math><mn>20</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi></math> from the convergent mirror, same size of the object
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
First refraction, u=-40 cm; f=+20 cm
From lens formula, 1v-1u=1f
1v-1-40=120⇒1v=120-140
v=+40 cm
m1=-1
First reflection, u=-20 cm;f=-10 cm
From mirror formula, 1v+1u=1f
1v-120=1-10
1v=1-10+120⇒v=-20 cm
m2=-1
Second refraction, u=-40 cm,  f=+20 cm
From lens formula, 1v-1-40=120⇒v=+40 cm
m3=-1
mtotal=m1×m2×m3=-1
Finally, image will be at distance 40 cm  from lens and is of same size as object.

questions.q: A photograph of a landscape is captured by a drone camera at a height of 18 km . The size of the camera film is $2 \mathrm{~cm} \times 2 \mathrm{~cm}$ and the area of the landscape photographed is $400 \mathrm{~km}^2$. The focal length of the lens in the drone camera is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\mathrm{H}=18 \mathrm{~km}$ Size of camera film $=2 \mathrm{~cm} \times 2 \mathrm{~cm}\begin{aligned} & A_{\text {image }}=400 \mathrm{~km}^2 \\ & x=20 \times 10^3 \mathrm{~m}=2 \times 10^4 \mathrm{~m} \\ & y=2 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{~m} \\ & \frac{x}{y}=10^6=\frac{18 \mathrm{Km}}{\mathrm{f}} \\ & \mathrm{f}=18 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m}=18 \mathrm{~mm} \\ & \mathrm{f}=1.8 \mathrm{~cm} \end{aligned}$

questions.q: If the distance between object and its two times magnified virtual image produced by a curved mirror is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>15</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>, the focal length of the mirror must be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: Since, image is magnified. So, it is a concave mirror. $\therefore \mathrm{m}=2=\frac{-\mathrm{v}}{\mathrm{u}}2=\frac{-(15-u)}{-u}2 u=15-u3 \mathrm{u}=15 \Rightarrow \mathrm{u}=5 \mathrm{~cm}\mathrm{v}=15-\mathrm{u}=15-5=10 \mathrm{~cm}$ Bymirror formula, $\frac{1}{\mathrm{f}}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{v}}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{u}}=\frac{1}{10}+\frac{1}{(-5)}=\frac{1-2}{10}=\frac{-1}{10}\mathrm{f}=-10 \mathrm{~cm}$

questions.q: A vessel of depth d is half filled with oil of refractive index n1 and the other half is filled with water of refractive index n2. The apparent depth of this vessel when viewed from above will be-
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The apparent depth formula is given by n=Real depthApparent depth.

The apparent depth in this case is given by 

d'=d1n1+d2n2⇒d'=d2(1n1+1n2)⇒d'=d2(n1+n2n1n2)

questions.q: The radius of curvature of each surface of a convex lens having refractive index <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>8</mn></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>. The lens is now immersed in a liquid of refractive index <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn></math>. The ratio of power of lens in air to its power in the liquid will be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>:</mo><mo> </mo><mn>1</mn></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The power of a lens is given by 

P1=1f

Using Lens Maker's formula,

P1=(1.8−1)1R1−1R2 and 

P2=1fimmersed =1.81.5−11R1−1R2

Hence, the ratio is,

P1P2=(1.8−1)1.81.5−1=0.8×1.50.3=4

questions.q: Two identical thin biconvex lenses of focal length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>15</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> and refractive index <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn></math> are in contact with each other. The space between the lenses is filled with a liquid of refractive index <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>25</mn></math>. The focal length of the combination is _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>cm</mi><mo>.</mo></math>
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For convex lenses, let radius of curvature is R. Then,

115 cm=1.5-11R-1-R

⇒1R=115 ⇒R=15 cm

Now for concave lens,

1fconcave=1.25-11-R-1R

=14×-2R=-130

1feff=115+115-130=-110

⇒feff=-10 cm

questions.q: The refractive index of prism is $\mu=\sqrt{3}$ and the ratio of the angle of minimum deviation to the angle of prism is one. The value of angle of prism is _______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For $\delta_{\min }\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{i}=\mathrm{e} \\ & \mathrm{r}_1=\mathrm{r}_2=\frac{\mathrm{A}}{2} \\ & \frac{\delta_{\min }}{\mathrm{A}}=1 \\ & \frac{2 \mathrm{i}-\mathrm{A}}{\mathrm{A}}=1 \\ & \\ & 2 \mathrm{i}=2 \mathrm{~A} \\ & \mathrm{i}=\mathrm{A} \end{aligned}$
Snell's law $\begin{aligned} & 1 \times \sin i=\mu \sin r \\ & \sin i=\mu \sin \left(\frac{A}{2}\right) \\ & \sin A=\mu \sin \left(\frac{A}{2}\right) \\ & 2 \sin \frac{A}{2} \cos \frac{A}{2}=\sqrt{3} \sin \left(\frac{A}{2}\right) \\ & \cos \left(\frac{A}{2}\right)=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\ & \therefore \frac{A}{2}=30^{\circ} \\ & \therefore A=60^{\circ} \end{aligned}$

questions.q: The driver sitting inside a parked car is watching vehicles approaching from behind with the help of his side view mirror, which is a convex mirror with radius of curvature $\mathrm{R}=2 \mathrm{~m}$. Another car approaches him from behind with a uniform speed of $90 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{hr}$. When the car is at a distance of 24 m from him, the magnitude of the acceleration of the image of the car in the side view mirror is ' a '. The value of 100 a is _______ $\mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}^2$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{v}=\frac{\mathrm{uf}}{\mathrm{u}-\mathrm{f}}=\frac{-24 \cdot 1}{-24-1}=\frac{24}{25} \\
& \mathrm{~m}=\frac{-\mathrm{v}}{\mathrm{u}}=-\frac{24}{25(-24)}=\frac{1}{25} \\
& \frac{1}{\mathrm{v}}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{u}}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{f}} \\
& \mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{I}}=-\mathrm{m}^2 \cdot \mathrm{v}_0=\frac{-1}{(25)^2} \cdot 25=\frac{-1}{25}
\end{aligned}$

Diff.
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{-1}{\mathrm{v}^2}\left(\frac{\mathrm{dv}}{\mathrm{dt}}\right)+\frac{1}{\mathrm{u}^2}\left(\frac{\mathrm{du}}{\mathrm{dt}}\right)=0\left[\frac{\mathrm{dv}}{\mathrm{dt}}=\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{i}} ; \frac{\mathrm{du}}{\mathrm{dt}}=\mathrm{v}_0\right] \\
& \frac{+2}{\mathrm{v}^3} \cdot\left(\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{t}}\right)^2-\frac{1}{\mathrm{v}^2} \cdot \mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{L}}-\frac{2}{\mathrm{u}^3} \cdot\left(\mathrm{v}_0\right)^2+\frac{1}{\mathrm{u}^2} \cdot \mathrm{a}_0=0 \\
& \frac{\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{I}}}{\mathrm{v}^2}=\frac{2}{\mathrm{v}^3} \cdot \mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{I}}^2-\frac{2}{\mathrm{u}^3} \cdot \mathrm{v}_0^2 \\
& \mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{I}}=\frac{2}{\mathrm{v}} \cdot \mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{I}}^2-\frac{2 \mathrm{v}^2}{\mathrm{u}^3} \cdot \mathrm{v}_0^2 \\
& =\frac{2 \cdot 25}{24} \cdot \frac{1}{25} \cdot \frac{1}{25}-\frac{2}{(24)^3} \cdot \frac{24}{25} \cdot \frac{24}{25} \cdot 25 \cdot 25 \\
& \mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{I}}=\frac{2}{24.25}-\frac{2}{24} \\
& \mathrm{a}_1=\frac{2}{24} \cdot \frac{-24}{25}=\frac{-2}{25} \\
& 100 a_1=\frac{2}{25} \times 100=8
\end{aligned}$
